topic: Databricks ai_decide: fast decisions over governed data
sourceTitle: Introducing ai_decide: make fast decisions on your governed data
summary: Databricks introduced ai_decide, an AI Function optimized for fast structured decisions rather than long-form generation, including routing, tagging and agent evaluation use cases.
whyItMatters: This is a strong educational topic because it exposes an architectural distinction between generation and decision workloads, with implications for latency, cost and governance.
angleSuggestions: When should you use a decision model instead of a generative LLM?
Why AI routing does not always need a large language model
The cost and latency case for specialized AI functions

topic: GPT-6 Sol and Luna arrive in Snowflake Cortex AI
sourceTitle: Announcing GPT-6 Sol and Luna on Snowflake Cortex AI
summary: Snowflake announced GPT-6 Sol and Luna in public preview through Cortex Inference, with calls running inside Snowflake's security and governance perimeter.
whyItMatters: This creates a useful architecture lesson around bringing frontier models to governed enterprise data instead of moving sensitive data out to separate AI stacks.
angleSuggestions: What changes when frontier inference lives inside the data platform?
Snowflake Cortex AI vs calling an external model endpoint directly
Governance boundaries for enterprise LLM inference

topic: Claude Sonnet 5.5: faster and cheaper than Sonnet 5
summary: Anthropic describes Claude Sonnet 5.5 as an upgrade over Sonnet 5 that runs 30% faster and costs up to 30% less for most work.
whyItMatters: The interesting lesson is not just a new model release; it is how architects should evaluate capability, latency and cost together before changing production defaults.
angleSuggestions: Why model upgrades should be evaluated on cost-performance, not benchmark hype
A practical model-upgrade checklist for enterprise teams
When a cheaper/faster model is the better production choice

topic: OpenAI Agents API: the harness becomes a managed platform primitive
summary: OpenAI introduced the Agents API in public beta for building and running cloud agents with a managed harness, including context management, tools, subagents and durable execution infrastructure.
whyItMatters: This is directly useful for explaining why production agents are more than an LLM loop: the harness, context, environment, tools and reliability layer are separate engineering concerns.
angleSuggestions: Why the agent loop is the easy part and the harness is the product
What a production agent harness actually needs
Managed agent infrastructure vs building your own harness

topic: How Databricks evaluates frontier models before rolling them out internally
sourceTitle: How Databricks rolls out frontier models to 12,000 employees on Day 1
summary: Databricks described its internal process for evaluating frontier models before company-wide rollout, emphasizing quality regression risk and cost controls rather than assuming every new model should become the default.
whyItMatters: This gives us a concrete, evidence-backed way to teach model governance, evaluation harnesses and rollout strategy rather than writing another generic model-comparison post.
